channel.title: MCP Monitor Daily Report
channel.description: Daily monitoring of Model Context Protocol mentions

item.title: Claude’s new MCP abilities feel useful - and a little loaded - PaPoo
item.description: Turns out a multi-agent harness with no authentication is a lovely way to hand your shell to whoever knocks first. Claude Code users, consider this your reminder to lock the doors.

item.title: Inside the Sovereign Publishing Machine: Pure-Rust MCP 2.0, Pelican (pocoo), Bluesky, and OmniLLL Studio
item.description: Turns out a publishing pipeline can be a daily ritual of Rust binaries, Pelican archives and MCP servers talking to each other, with the browser reduced to a spectator.

item.title: A free MCP security scanner is appealing - but I’d still treat it like a first pass - PaPoo
item.description: Zero trust sounds tidy on paper, but shared agent memory is messy, partial, and socially negotiated. Provenance is the unglamorous detail that actually matters.

item.title: The agent tax has arrived: Google Workspace's MCP pricing - Martin Alderson
item.description: Google has discovered that agents are customers too, and they would like to be billed accordingly. Apps read your inbox for free, agents pay twenty cents a thousand.

item.title: Flowmaps | The Logic Layer for Agents and Developers
item.description: Flowmaps lets an agent trace every business flow touching a billing function before it touches the code, which is more diligence than most of us bring to a Friday checkout bug.

item.title: GitHub - calypso-so/elephant-mcp: Elephant by Calypso: MCP server for your team's knowledge. Hosted (Streamable HTTP, OAuth) or local over stdio via npm. · GitHub
item.description: Your documents, finally talking back, one citation at a time. Elephant plugs into any MCP-speaking assistant and refuses to answer what your files don't say.

item.title: How we reduced our MCP server's context window usage by up to 267x
item.description: Turns out handing an agent every GitHub API operation at once is a bit like giving a new hire the entire company wiki on day one. Ranking fixed that.

item.title: Let your AI assistant run SQL on 36 real database engines: the sqlize.online MCP server - DEV Community
item.description: Turns out MySQL quietly treats || as logical OR, which is exactly the kind of thing a model should run before it confidently tells you otherwise.

item.title: GitHub - marciob/grok-x-mcp: Search X from ChatGPT, Claude or Gemini through your own Grok Bot. A self-hosted MCP server with no dependencies. · GitHub
item.description: Grok Bot already knows how to search X, so this server simply hands that ability to whichever chat app you prefer, with an OAuth handshake and a webhook round trip in between.

item.title: Why I'm Bullish on MCP for 2027 | Philschmid
item.description: MCP had its backlash, then quietly kept growing. Now it's picking up Code Mode, Skills, Events, and embedded UI, and the author is betting on it for 2027.

item.title: Best Web search MCP servers (November 2026) · tested every night
item.description: A leaderboard of web search MCP servers, re-tested every night, where the scores are mostly about how cheaply and reliably each server speaks the protocol.

item.title: Bloque - All Your MCPs, Centrally Managed.
item.description: Scattered MCP servers, meet your new control tower. One endpoint, one key, and suddenly your whole team is on the same page.

item.title: MCP Servers Now Carry Their Own Playbooks, and That Changes How Agents Use Tools | DevOps.com
item.description: Turns out the tool itself can now tell the AI how to behave, which is either a handy onboarding feature or a new thing for security teams to worry about.

item.title: Planet News Roundup - openSUSE News
item.description: This week openSUSE let AI assistants start installing your operating system, with safety rails and the feature switched off by default. Mostly reassuring, a little bit terrifying.

item.title: Skills over MCP: what changed and what admins should check first | Pondero
item.description: Connecting an MCP server used to mean approving its tools. Now it also means approving the playbook it hands Claude, and the default settings deserve a second look.

item.title: BOTERNITY log, 2026-11-26
item.description: Turns out a lot of public MCP servers are either sleeping, sprawling in their token budgets, or quietly rewriting their tool definitions at night. Your agent's context window sends its regards.

item.title: Capturing agent intent - Docs - PostHog
item.description: Ever wondered why your AI agent just pressed that button? PostHog's SDK asks the agent politely, then sneaks in a backup plan if it doesn't answer.

item.title: #anthropic #mcp #claude #tracetrim #ai #genai #generativeai #intelligenzaartificiale #llm | Alessio Pomaro
item.description: MCP servers can now hand agents a instruction manual along with the tools, so nobody has to read the fine print anymore. Probably a relief for everyone involved.

item.title: CoinGecko MCP - MCP server for crypto | TradingAIHub
item.description: Your AI assistant can now check the price of anything on CoinGecko without you leaving the chat, provided you remember to paste one URL in the right settings menu.

item.title: Brokers Are Opening Accounts to AI Agents. Here's What Each One Lets Them Do | TradingAIHub
item.description: Four brokers gave AI assistants the keys over MCP, and each decided differently how much those keys should open. Reading the fine print turns out to matter more than the launch headlines.

item.title: Official vs Community MCP Servers for Finance: How to Tell Them Apart | TradingAIHub
item.description: Turns out a server named after a big brokerage isn't always made by it. This guide shows how to check who really publishes your finance MCP tools before you hand them your account.
